chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Yunus, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:
'The Momin brings tranquility to the Momin just as the thirsty one finds tranquility in the cold water.'

key_terms.الظَّمْآنُ: the intensely thirsty one — a person whose need for water is acute and urgent, used as a simile for the believer's yearning for a fellow believer
key_terms.الْمَاءِ الْبَارِدِ: cold water — the immediate and perfect relief for intense thirst; the point of comparison (wajh al-shabah) for the solace a believer provides to another
key_terms.الْمُؤْمِنَ: the believer (Momin) — one possessed of true iman; the subject whose presence brings spiritual comfort and repose to a fellow believer
key_terms.لَيَسْكُنُ: finds tranquility, settles into stillness, is calmed — conveys deep inner peace and the cessation of restlessness

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq (AS) say about the tranquility and bond that believers find in one another according to al-Kafi?
ai.summary: In this hadith, Imam Abu Abdullah Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) describes the profound spiritual and emotional bond between believers through a vivid simile: just as a person burning with intense thirst finds immediate relief and perfect solace upon reaching cold water, so too does a believer find natural comfort, peace, and tranquility in the presence of a fellow believer. The hadith elevates the bond of iman between the faithful beyond mere social affiliation to one of deep spiritual kinship and mutual repose.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa Bin Ubeyud, from Yunus, from the one who mentioned it, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The Momin brings tranquillity to the Momin just as the thirsty one gets tranquilled to the cold water’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa ibn ‘Ubayd from Yunus from those he has mentioned (in his book) from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “
A believer finds comfort with another believer just as a thirsty person finds relief from cool water.”
